statement_tex:

label: thm:main
statement_tex:
\label{thm:main}
    Let $f: \ \RR^d \longrightarrow \RR$ be represented by a rank-$k$ Maxout multiplication network.
    Then it can be written as an exact difference $f = g - h$ of two rank-$\max\{k,2\}$ Maxout multiplication networks, whose downstream maps are monotone in the non-negative split inputs $x^+=\max\{x,0\}$ and $x^-=\max\{-x,0\}$. The constructed functions need not be convex in $x$.
    For fixed rank and uniformly bounded total multiplication degree $\sum_u w^{uv}$, the construction has linear size in the original graph size (counting arcs as well as neurons). A bound on the number of distinct inputs alone does not bound the number $\prod_u(w^{uv}+1)$ of binomial summands.
scope: Actual finite shared Maxout/product DAG with arbitrary signed affine weights/biases and natural exponents. Constructed positive rank-two DAG has exact all-node recovery, monotonicity on nonnegative split inputs and finite maxima of nonnegative-coefficient ordinary polynomials; explicit vertices-plus-arcs size bound C(K,D) times source size under fixed rank and bounded total multiplication degree. Canonical input recovery is explicit; raw-input splitting is a separate preprocessing map.

The Stopping Game allows a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium, unique up to tie-breaking at

label: def:adf-game-states
statement_tex:
[Stopping Game State Space]\label{def:adf-game-states} The game is played on the following states:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Activation States:} $s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}$ where layer $l \in \{1, \dots, L\}$ and
        player $q \in \{+,-\}$ is in turn at neuron $j$.
    \item \textbf{Terminal States:} $s_{k,q}^{(0)}$ where $k$ is an input dimension and $q \in \{+,-\}$ is
        the final turn label.
    \item \textbf{Cemetery State:} $\dagger$, an absorbing state reached upon stopping.
\end{itemize}
We adopt the convention that, when a transition kernel or recursion at layer $l$ references the
predecessor state $s_{i,r}^{(l-1, \mathrm{act})}$, the symbol denotes the activation state at layer
$l-1 \ge 1$ as defined above and, in the boundary case $l = 1$, is interpreted as the terminal
state $s_{i,r}^{(0)}$.

label: def:adf-recursion
statement_tex:
[Payoffs, Transitions, and Value Recursion]\label{def:adf-recursion}
Fix an input $x$.

\textbf{Payoffs.} The player-specific \emph{payoff} $r_p$ at activation states is paid out
depending on the action chosen by the active player, and paid out at terminal and cemetery states
without prerequisites:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Cemetery: $r_p(\dagger) \coloneqq 0$.
    \item Active state: $r_p(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}, \mathrm{stop}) \coloneqq 0$ (stopping pays nothing)
        and $r_p(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}, \mathrm{cont}) \coloneqq b_j^{(l, p \oplus q)}$ (continuation
        pays a positive bias to the active player $q$---covered by the case $p \oplus q = +$---and the
        absolute value of a negative bias to its opponent $q'$---covered by the case $p \oplus q = -$).
    \item Terminal: $r_p(s_{k,q}^{(0)}) \coloneqq x_k^{p \oplus q}$ (at terminal states the payoff depends on
        state only---the game ends here. A positive input is paid to the active player $q$---covered by the
        case $p \oplus q = +$---whereas the absolute value of a negative input is paid to its opponent
        $q'$---covered by the case $p \oplus q = -$).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Transition kernel.} Stopping at state $s^{(l, \text{act})}_{j,p}$ deterministically sends
the game to the cemetery; continuation transports backward by one layer with transition
probabilities depending on the fraction of the respective absolute network weight compared to the
sum of absolute incoming weights at neuron $j$ of layer $l$. In case of a positive weight, the
active player $p$ stays in turn, in case of a negative weight, the turn switches to its opponent
$p'$.
\begin{align}\label{eq:adf-kernel-stop}
    \P\bigl(\dagger \,\big|\, s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}, \mathrm{stop}\bigr) \coloneqq 1,
\end{align}
\begin{align}\label{eq:adf-kernel}
    \P\bigl(s_{i,r}^{(l-1, \mathrm{act})} \,\big|\, s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}, \mathrm{cont}\bigr)
    \coloneqq \frac{W_{ij}^{(l, q \oplus r)}}{\gamma_j^{(l)}},
    \qquad
    \gamma_j^{(l)} \coloneqq \sum_i \bigl(W_{ij}^{(l,+)} + W_{ij}^{(l,-)}\bigr) = \sum_i
    \bigl|W_{ij}^{(l)}\bigr|,
\end{align}
where $\gamma_j^{(l)}$ is the local structural discount that restores unit row-sum (if
$\gamma_j^{(l)} = 0$, continuation leads to $\dagger$). For understanding the idea of the
occupation measure, we remark that those $\gamma^{(l)}_j$ are going to weight the trajectories in
the occupation measure.

\textbf{Policy.} A pure, i.e., deterministic policy $\pi = (\pi_+, \pi_-)$ assigns each active
state $s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}$ a binary stop/continue decision by the player in turn,
\begin{align}
    \pi_q\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}\bigr) \in \{0, 1\},
    \qquad
    1 = \mathrm{cont},\ 0 = \mathrm{stop}.
\end{align}
\textbf{Player-specific action and game values.} For each policy $\pi$, the player-specific
\textbf{action value} $\tilde{Q}_p^\pi(s, a)$ is the expected discounted payoff for player $p$
starting at $s$ with action $a$ and following $\pi$ thereafter, defined by the standard Bellman
equation
\begin{align}\label{eq:adf-q-bellman}
    \tilde{Q}_p^\pi(s, a) \coloneqq r_p(s, a) + \gamma(s)\, \textstyle\sum_{s'} \P\bigl(s' \,\big|\, s,
    a\bigr)\, \tilde{V}_p^\pi(s'),
\end{align}
where $\tilde{V}_p^\pi$ is the player-specific game value defined below. We use tildes to reserve
$V_p^\pi$ for the advantage further down, which already carries a subtracted $\tilde{V}_{p'}^\pi$.
At active states~\eqref{eq:adf-q-bellman} specializes,
using~\eqref{eq:adf-kernel-stop}--\eqref{eq:adf-kernel}, to
\begin{align}\label{eq:adf-q-stop}
    \tilde{Q}_p^\pi\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})},\, \mathrm{stop}\bigr) &= 0 + 1 \cdot
    \tilde{V}_p^\pi(\dagger) = 0 \\ \label{eq:adf-q-cont}
    \tilde{Q}_p^\pi\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})},\, \mathrm{cont}\bigr)
    &= b_j^{(l, p \oplus q)} + \gamma_j^{(l)} \textstyle\sum_{s'} \P\bigl(s' \,\big|\, s_{j,q}^{(l,
    \mathrm{act})}, \mathrm{cont}\bigr)\, \tilde{V}_p^\pi(s') \\
    &= b_j^{(l, p \oplus q)} + \sum_{i,r} W_{ij}^{(l, q \oplus r)}\,
    \tilde{V}_p^\pi\bigl(s_{i,r}^{(l-1, \mathrm{act})}\bigr).
\end{align}
The \textbf{player-specific game value} $\tilde{V}_p^\pi(s)$ is the action value averaged by the
policy. At terminal and cemetery states it equals the local payoff there:
\begin{align}\label{eq:adf-v-terminal}
    \tilde{V}_p^\pi\bigl(s_{k,q}^{(0)}\bigr) \coloneqq x_k^{p \oplus q},
    \qquad
    \tilde{V}_p^\pi(\dagger) \coloneqq 0.
\end{align}
At active states,
\begin{align}\label{eq:adf-v-active}
    \tilde{V}_p^\pi\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}\bigr) \coloneqq \pi_q\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l,
    \mathrm{act})}\bigr)\, \tilde{Q}_p^\pi\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})},\, \mathrm{cont}\bigr) +
    \bigl(1 - \pi_q\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}\bigr)\bigr)\, \tilde{Q}_p^\pi\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l,
    \mathrm{act})},\, \mathrm{stop}\bigr).
\end{align}
Since $\pi_q$ is binary,~\eqref{eq:adf-v-active} selects either $\tilde{Q}_p^\pi(\cdot,
    \mathrm{cont})$ or $\tilde{Q}_p^\pi(\cdot, \mathrm{stop}) = 0$.

\textbf{Game value.} The quantity the player in turn maximizes at each active state is the
advantage of player $p$ at $s$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:adf-advantage}
    V_p^\pi(s) \coloneqq \tilde{V}_p^\pi(s) - \tilde{V}_{p'}^\pi(s).
\end{align}

label: rem:adf-spne-uniqueness
statement_tex:
[Uniqueness of the SPNE up to tie-breaking] \label{rem:adf-spne-uniqueness}
It is easy to see in the following proof that the SPNE \eqref{eq:adf-spne-policy} is unique up to
tie-breaking at states where continuing yields zero advantage $\tilde
    Q_q^{\pi^\star}(\cdot,\mathrm{cont})-\tilde Q_{q'}^{\pi^\star}(\cdot,\mathrm{cont}) = z_j^{(l)} =
    0$---representing neurons of preactivation zero. The pinned Stopping-Game attribution code selects continuation at exact zero in its hard backward mask, while the Routing Game and Hellinger diagnostic use strict positivity. These choices give the same original forward activation at a tie but can give different selected backward quantities there. The theorem here uses stopping at ties. We refer to the policy
\eqref{eq:adf-spne-policy} by \textbf{stop-at-tie-breaks} equilibrium.

label: def:addition-subgame
statement_tex:
[Addition Oracle]\label{def:addition-subgame}
For a residual node $z = x + y$, the \emph{addition state} $s_{z,q}^{\mathrm{add}}$ has active
player $q \in \{+,-\}$ and operand states $s_{x,q}, s_{y,q}$ at the two summands. The transition
kernel is the uniform Oracle
\begin{align}
    \P\bigl(s_{x,q} \,\big|\, s_{z,q}^{\mathrm{add}}\bigr) \coloneqq \tfrac{1}{2},
    \qquad
    \P\bigl(s_{y,q} \,\big|\, s_{z,q}^{\mathrm{add}}\bigr) \coloneqq \tfrac{1}{2},
\end{align}
with player $q$ retained at the chosen operand. The immediate payoff is
$r_p(s_{z,q}^{\mathrm{add}}) \coloneqq 0$ for both $p \in \{+,-\}$, and the structural discount is
$\gamma_{\mathrm{O}} \coloneqq 2$.

label: def:trajectory-distribution
statement_tex:
[Game trajectory and trajectory law]\label{def:trajectory-distribution}
Fix an input $x$ and a root state $s$. A \emph{game trajectory} rooted at $s$ is a finite sequence
of game states
\begin{align}
    \zeta \;=\; (\zeta_0, \zeta_1, \dots, \zeta_T), \qquad \zeta_0 = s,
\end{align}
that follows the admissible transitions of the game (Definition~\ref{def:adf-recursion} together
with the addition/max-pooling Oracle splits of
Definitions~\ref{def:addition-subgame}--\ref{def:maxpool-subgame}) until it terminates either at a
layer-$0$ terminal state $\zeta_T = s_{k,r}^{(0)}$ (reaching an input dimension $k$) or at the
cemetery state $\zeta_T = \dagger$ (reached the first time a player chooses \emph{stop}). The set
of all such trajectories is the trajectory \emph{ground set} $\mathcal{T}_s$. Composing the
transition kernel~\eqref{eq:adf-kernel-stop}--\eqref{eq:adf-kernel}, the Oracle splits, and a
(possibly stochastic) policy $\pi$ at every activation state defines a Markov kernel on game
states, which together with the deterministic start at $s$ induces a probability distribution
$\Pi_x^\pi(\cdot \mid s)$ on $\mathcal{T}_s$. Trajectories that pass through closed gates---neurons
$j$ with $\1[z_j^{(l)} > 0] = 0$---are admissible elements of $\mathcal{T}_s$, but under the
equilibrium policy $\pi^\star$ the player at the activation state stops there, so any trajectory
continuing past a closed gate carries probability zero. We write $\Pi_x(\cdot \mid s) \coloneqq
    \Pi_x^{\pi^\star}(\cdot \mid s)$ for the equilibrium \emph{trajectory law} and $\Pi_x \coloneqq
    \Pi_x(\cdot \mid s_0)$ for the law rooted at the output state $s_0 \coloneqq
    s_{u,+}^{(L,\mathrm{act})}$.
scope: Finite recursive walk law and normalization for stochastic kernels.

label: def:occupation
statement_tex:
[Discounted Occupation Measure]\label{def:occupation}
Let $\Pi_x(\cdot \mid s)$ be the equilibrium trajectory law of
Definition~\ref{def:trajectory-distribution}.
Define the cumulative discount
\begin{align}
    d_t(\zeta) \coloneqq \prod_{m=0}^{t-1} \gamma(\zeta_m), \qquad d_0(\zeta) = 1,
\end{align}
where $\gamma(\zeta_m) = \gamma_{\mathrm{O}} = 2$ for addition Oracle states, $\gamma(\zeta_m) =
    \gamma_{\mathrm{O}} = 1$ for max-pooling states, and $\gamma(\zeta_m) = \gamma_j^{(l)}$ for
continuation at activation states $\zeta_m = s_{j,q}^{(l,\mathrm{act})}$ (per-neuron
weight-magnitude discount). The \emph{discounted occupation measure} of state $v$ for trajectories
rooted at $s$ is
\begin{align}
    \Gamma_x(v \mid s) \coloneq \E_{\zeta \sim \Pi_x(\cdot \mid s)}\left[\sum_t d_t(\zeta)\,\1\{\zeta_t
    = v\}\right],
    \qquad
    \Gamma_x(v) \coloneqq \Gamma_x(v \mid s_0).
\end{align}

label: def:routing-recursion
statement_tex:
[Entropy-Regularized Two-Player Routing Game]\label{def:routing-recursion}
Fix an input $x$ and a stabilizer $\varepsilon \ge 0$. At each activation state $s_{j,p}^{(l,
    act)}$, the player in turn chooses \emph{stop} or \emph{continue} with similar mechanics as in the
Stopping Game (Appendix~\ref{app:relu-net-game}) reflecting the open-closed state of a ReLU gate:
stopping sends the game to the cemetery $\dagger$ giving immediate payoff $\ell(0) = -\infty$---and
continuation transitions backward with structural discount $\gamma=2$ and the uniform $1/2$
sign-branch kernel given above. Here happens the critical step: gains of the opponent on the
negative stream state $s_{j,p',-}^{(l, \text{lin})}$ shall be counted as losses of the active
player $p$. At each linear routing state $s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)}$, the player in turn instead
chooses a mixed action $\nu \in \Delta(\mathrm{Pred}_j^{(l)} \cup \{\mathrm{bias},
    \perp_{\mathrm{lin}}\})$ over the predecessors of neuron $j$ augmented by a terminal \emph{bias
node} with immediate payoff $\ell([b_j^{(l)}]^\kappa)$ and a fictitious \emph{outside option}
$\perp_{\mathrm{lin}}$ which routes the game's mass to the cemetery with immediate payoff $\ell
    (\varepsilon)$; trajectories entering either are absorbed. Let $\mathcal{H}(\nu) \coloneqq
    -\sum_{a} \nu(a)\log \nu(a)$ be Shannon entropy over this augmented action set. At $\varepsilon =
    0$ the outside option carries $\ell (0) = -\infty$ and is dominated by every positive-mass
predecessor, so the augmented game reduces to the Routing Game over $\mathrm{Pred}_j^{(l)} \cup
    \{\mathrm{bias}\}$.

An admissible profile chooses a pure stop/continue action at each activation state and a probability vector at each linear routing state. Under any profile, evaluate the displayed recursions using those choices, without taking maxima: use the chosen activation action and the chosen routing vector's expected log score plus entropy. A zero-probability term contributes zero even when its score is $-\infty$; positive probability on a $-\infty$ score makes the routing value $-\infty$.

Throughout, $\mathbf{V}(\cdot) = (V_p(\cdot), V_{p'}(\cdot))^\top$ denotes the game's
backward-induction player-specific log-value function, defined jointly at linear routing states
by~\eqref{eq:routing-linear-value} and at activation states by~\eqref{eq:routing-activation-value}
below. The recursion is well-posed because the layered state graph is a finite DAG: the $l=1$ case
of~\eqref{eq:routing-linear-action} needs no lower-layer $\mathbf{V}$, and every subsequent layer
uses only $\mathbf{V}$ at strictly lower layers.

For a \textbf{linear routing state} at $l \geq 2$ the active player continuing to the $i$th
neuron's activation state receives an immediate payoff of the logarithm of the respective weight
summed with the respective log-value function of the next state, whereas in the first layer the
final payoff is paid out to the active player. The inactive player always obtains an immediate
payoff of $\ell(0) = -\infty$. Let us denote by $Q_r(s, a)$ player $r$'s gain for the game value in
case action $a$ actually happens, whereas $\bar Q_r$ denotes the mixture of the differences between
the payoffs of the opponents including the entropy regularization term given the mixed strategy
chosen by the active player.
\begin{align}\label{eq:routing-linear-action}
    Q_r \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)}, i \bigr)
    \coloneqq
    \begin{cases}
        \ell\!\bigl(W_{ij}^{(l,\kappa)}\bigr) + V_r\bigl(s_{i,q}^{(l-1, act)}\bigr), & r=q,\ l \ge 2,\\[0.35em]
        \ell\!\bigl([x_iW_{ij}^{(1)}]^\kappa\bigr), & r=q,\ l = 1,\\[0.35em]
        -\infty, & r=q'.
    \end{cases}
\end{align}
The outside option $\perp_{\mathrm{lin}}$ and the bias node have log-scores
$Q_r(s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l,\mathrm{lin})}, \perp_{\mathrm{lin}}) \coloneqq \ell(\varepsilon)$ and
$Q_r(s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l,\mathrm{lin})}, \mathrm{bias}) \coloneqq \ell([b_j^{(l)}]^\kappa)$ for $r =
    q$ and $-\infty$ for $r = q'$; they route the $\varepsilon$-fraction and the bias share of the mass
to absorbing terminals instead of to any predecessor.
If player $q$ uses mixed action $\nu$ at this state, the induced \emph{individual routed masses}
are
\begin{align}\label{eq:optimal-linear}
    \bar Q_r \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)};\nu \bigr)
    &\coloneqq
    \sum_a \nu(a)\, \ell \left( \exp \left( Q_r \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)}, a \bigr) \right) -
    \exp \left( Q_{r'} \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)}, a \bigr) \right) \right) \notag\\
    &\quad + \tau \mathcal{H}(\nu),
    \qquad r \in \{q,q'\},
\end{align}
which, as $\exp(-\infty)=0$, evaluates to
\begin{align}
    \bar Q_q \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)};\nu \bigr)
    &=
    \sum_a \nu(a)\, Q_q \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)}, a \bigr)
    + \tau \mathcal{H}(\nu) \\
    \bar Q_{q'} \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)};\nu \bigr)
    &= -\infty.
\end{align}
If $W_{ij}^{(l,\kappa)} = 0$ for every predecessor $i$ and $[b_j^{(l)}]^\kappa = 0$ (i.e.\ the
stream-$\kappa$ part of the fan-in to neuron $j$ is identically zero), then
$Q_q(s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l,\mathrm{lin})},i) = -\infty$ for all $i$ as well and the
value~\eqref{eq:routing-linear-value} equals $\ell(\varepsilon)$. If $\varepsilon=0$ and every
action scores $-\infty$ (e.g.\ $\Sigma_j^{(l,\kappa)}=0$ at $\tau=1$), every $\nu$ is a best
response; we fix $\nu=\delta_{\perp_{\mathrm{lin}}}$ (absorption), matching the convention
$0/0\coloneqq0$ in~\eqref{eq:lrp-eps-recursion}.
We define the corresponding equilibrium linear-game values by
\begin{align}\label{eq:routing-linear-value}
    V^\star_q \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)} \bigr)
    &\coloneqq
    \max_{\nu \in \Delta(\mathrm{Pred}_j^{(l)} \cup \{\mathrm{bias}, \perp_{\mathrm{lin}}\})}
    \bar Q_q\bigl(s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)};\nu\bigr) \nonumber \\
    &=
    \max_{\nu \in \Delta(\mathrm{Pred}_j^{(l)} \cup \{\mathrm{bias}, \perp_{\mathrm{lin}}\})}
    \left\{
    \sum_{a} \nu(a)\, Q_q \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)}, a \bigr)
    + \tau \mathcal{H}(\nu)
    \right\} \nonumber \\
    &=
    \tau \cdot \ell \left( \varepsilon^{ \frac{1}{\tau} } +
    \bigl([b_j^{(l)}]^\kappa\bigr)^{\frac{1}{\tau}} + \sum_i \exp\left( Q_q(s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)},
    i) \right)^{ \frac{ 1 }{ \tau } } \right), \\
    V^\star_{q'} \bigl( s_{j,q,\kappa}^{(l, lin)} \bigr)
    &\coloneqq -\infty,
\end{align}
where we used~\eqref{eq:gibbs-lse}. At $\tau = 1$ the associated Gibbs policy assigns the outside
option the probability $\varepsilon / (\varepsilon + \sum_{a \neq \perp_{\mathrm{lin}}} \exp
    Q_q(\cdots, a))$ and distributes the remaining mass over the predecessors and the bias node in
proportion to $\exp Q_q$.

For an \textbf{activation state}, continuing exposes both sign branches. Let $s_+ \coloneqq
    s_{j,p,+}^{(l, \text{lin})}$ and $s_- \coloneqq s_{j,p',-}^{(l, \text{lin})}$. If player $p$
chooses \emph{continue} at $s_{j,p}^{(l, act)}$, the game transitions to $s_+$ or to $s_-$ with
equal probability, while \emph{stop} sends the game to the cemetery with game value
$V_r(\dagger)=\ell(0)=-\infty$. Taking the expectation over the uniform sign-branch kernel
($\frac{1}{2}$ each) and respecting the discount $\gamma_O = 2$ interpreted in logarithmic space,
the continuation value becomes
\begin{align}\label{eq:routing-activation-continue}
    Q_r \bigl( s_{j,p}^{(l, act)}, \mathrm{continue} \bigr)
    &\coloneqq
    \ell \left( \sum_{s' \in \{s_+, s_-\}} \P(s' \mid s_{j,p}^{(l, act)}) \cdot \gamma_{\mathrm{O}}
    \cdot \Bigl( \exp V_r(s') - \exp V_{r'}(s') \Bigr) \right) \nonumber \\
    &= \ell \left(
    \xi_{r,p} \Bigl( \exp\left( V_p\left( s_+ \right) \right) - \exp\left( V_{p'}\left( s_- \right)
    \right) \Bigr)
    \right).
\end{align}

Stopping yields $-\infty$ for both players. We select \emph{stop at every activation-state tie in log space}, so the selected policy and active-player value are
\begin{align}\label{eq:routing-activation-value}
    \pi_p^\star(\mathrm{continue}\mid s_{j,p}^{(l,\mathrm{act})})
    &\coloneqq \1\!\left[Q_p(s_{j,p}^{(l,\mathrm{act})},\mathrm{continue})>-\infty\right],\\
    V_p(s_{j,p}^{(l,\mathrm{act})})
    &\coloneqq \max\{-\infty,Q_p(s_{j,p}^{(l,\mathrm{act})},\mathrm{continue})\}.
\end{align}
Writing $D_p=\exp V_p(s_+)-\exp V_{p'}(s_-)$, this selects continuing exactly when $D_p>0$. When $D_p\leq0$, both actions have log value $-\infty$ and the convention selects stopping. If continuing is selected, the opponent's continuation value is $-\infty$; if stopping is selected, both players receive $-\infty$. Thus in either case
\begin{align}
    V_{p'}(s_{j,p}^{(l,\mathrm{act})})=-\infty.
\end{align}

label: rem:routing-spne-uniqueness
statement_tex:
[Uniqueness]\label{rem:routing-spne-uniqueness}
The linear-state Gibbs best response~\eqref{eq:routing-spne-linear} is the unique maximizer of the
strictly concave entropy-regularized objective whenever some action has a finite score (otherwise
Definition~\ref{def:routing-recursion} fixes $\perp_{\mathrm{lin}}$). At activation states the active player is indifferent whenever the signed continuation mass $\exp V_p(s_+) - \exp V_{p'}(s_-)$ is nonpositive ($z_j^{(l)}\leq0$ at $\tau=1$), because both log-space action values are then $-\infty$. Thus the unconstrained best-response set can contain several policies. The theorem specifies the
tie-breaker $\pi_p^\star = \1[Q_p(\cdot,\mathrm{continue}) > -\infty]$, which at $\tau=1$ reduces
to $\1[z_j^{(l)} > 0]$. Just like in the \ac{SG} (Appendix~\ref{app:relu-net-game}), we refer to
this SPNE as the \textbf{stop-at-tie-breaks} equilibrium. This canonical choice also selects the absorbing outside action whenever every routing action has zero mass; without these conventions, both activation log ties and empty routing streams permit multiple optimal choices.

statement_tex:

canonical convention that the game starts at the $+$-state.

and the per-neuron \emph{sum} $\Gamma^{(l)}_j = \Gamma_x(s_{j,+}^{(l,\mathrm{act})}) +
    \Gamma_x(s_{j,-}^{(l,\mathrm{act})})$ in place of~\eqref{eq:routing-Gamma-pair}. We have chosen the
non-negative-discount version because it is easier to comprehend---$\Gamma_x$ remains a genuine
non-negative occupation measure, and the LRP sign is generated by an explicit algebraic difference
rather than absorbed into the trajectory weights.

label: rem:noisy-gate-perception
statement_tex:
[Optimal policy under perceived payoff noise]\label{rem:noisy-gate-perception}
The optimum $\pi^\star = \Phi(z_i^{(l)})$ admits an equivalent interpretation as the marginal of an
optimal pure rule: the player perceives the continuation payoff at $s_{i,q}^{(l)}$ as the noisy
quantity $z_i^{(l)} + \eta$ with $\eta \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$ independent across states, and
applies the noiseless-optimal pure rule \emph{``continue iff the perceived payoff is strictly
positive''} on this perception. Marginalizing the rule over $\eta$ at fixed $z_i^{(l)}$ recovers
the continue probability,
\begin{align}\label{eq:noisy-gate-marginal}
    \P_{\eta\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)}\!\bigl(z_i^{(l)} + \eta > 0\bigr) \;=\; \Phi(z_i^{(l)}).
\end{align}
The realized continuation payoff is the deterministic $z_i^{(l)}$ from the actual network forward
pass: the noise $\eta$ lives in the player's perception of the payoff while the environment pays
out $z_i^{(l)}$ on continuation, so the expected backward Bellman comparison at $s_{i,q}^{(l)}$ is
the soft mass $\Phi(z_i^{(l)}) \cdot z_i^{(l)}$ in place of the deterministic $\1[z_i^{(l)} >
    0]\cdot z_i^{(l)}$.

label: thm:softplus-forward
statement_tex:
[Softplus forward equivalence]\label{thm:softplus-forward}
The entropy-regularized Stopping Game of~\eqref{eq:softplus-soft-bellman} admits an SPNE whose
activation-state policy is the Gibbs policy~\eqref{eq:softplus-policy}; it is unique on networks
without max-pooling nodes, since~\eqref{eq:softplus-soft-bellman} is strictly concave (ties at
max-pooling states are resolved as in Appendix~\ref{app:notation-identities}). Under this
equilibrium, at every activation state $s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}$,
\begin{align}\label{eq:softplus-spne-tildes}
    \tilde V_p^{\pi^\star}\!\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}\bigr)
    \;=\;
    a_{\mathrm{soft},j}^{(l, p \oplus q,\,\theta)},
    \qquad
    V_q^{\pi^\star}\!\bigl(s_{j,q}^{(l, \mathrm{act})}\bigr)
    \;=\;
    \mathrm{sp}_\theta\!\bigl(z_j^{(l)}\bigr),
\end{align}
where $a_{\mathrm{soft},j}^{(l, \pm,\,\theta)}$ are the Softplus-Decomposition activations of the
Softplus network with activation $\mathrm{sp}_\theta$, propagated
by~\eqref{eq:split-pos}--\eqref{eq:split-neg} from $a_{\mathrm{soft},k}^{(0,\pm,\theta)} = x_k^\pm$
with the decomposition function
\begin{align}\label{eq:softplus-decomp}
    f_{\mathrm{soft}}^{\,\theta}(z^+, z^-) \;\coloneqq\; \bigl(\,\mathrm{sp}'_\theta(z^+ - z^-)\, z^+ +
    \theta\, \mathcal{H}_\theta(z^+ - z^-),\;\; \mathrm{sp}'_\theta(z^+ - z^-)\, z^-\,\bigr),
\end{align}
and $\mathcal{H}_\theta(z) \coloneqq \mathcal{H}(\mathrm{sp}'_\theta(z))$ the binary entropy of the
Gibbs weight.

label: rem:rg-natural-equivalence
statement_tex:
[Routing-state elimination and absorption histories]\label{rem:rg-natural-equivalence}
The refined diagnostic routing process just defined alternates activation and linear-routing states.
A dead activation stops at the gate substep; an alive activation chooses its
$\kappa$ branch uniformly, after which an empty branch or outside option can
absorb at the routing substep. The refined layered process retains these
substeps and pads the cemetery state after absorption. Algorithm~\ref{alg:hellinger}
applies to this expanded state graph; the diagnostics are read at the activation
boundaries. This is the process implemented by the separate gate and branch
absorption updates.

For a trajectory that remains ordinary, deleting each intermediate routing
state is a bijection: its neuron and player are determined by the adjacent
activation states, and its branch by whether the player is kept or switched
(or by the pixel-stream tag at the input). The act-to-act formulas therefore
preserve ordinary surviving-path probabilities and their Bhattacharyya overlap.
The same applies after conditioning both laws on survival.

For absorbing trajectories, deletion need not be injective: a gate stop and a
later empty-branch stop can become the same act-only trajectory. Thus full-law
Bhattacharyya and Hellinger equality is asserted only when absorption histories
are recoverable, for example when no alive routing branch leaks to the cemetery.
In general the finite-fibre Cauchy--Schwarz inequality gives
\[
 \mathrm{BC}_{\mathrm{refined}}\leq\mathrm{BC}_{\mathrm{act\text{-}only}},
 \qquad
 \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{refined}}\geq\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{act\text{-}only}}.
\]
For example, take one input $x=1$ and weight $W=1$. Model $A$ has bias $0$ and
continues, with its empty negative branch absorbing with probability $1/2$;
model $B$ has bias $-2$ and stops at the gate. Their refined path supports are
disjoint, so $\mathrm{BC}_{\mathrm{refined}}=0$. Collapsing the two absorption
substeps instead gives $\mathrm{BC}_{\mathrm{act\text{-}only}}=1/\sqrt2$.
scope: Corrected finite-law coarsening inequalities, exact reindexing with an erase/recover inverse, and normalized explicit absorption-history counterexample. Equality for the model survivor graph requires its stated reconstruction property.

Suppose a dead state sends all its mass to the cemetery. Every state in the
alive symmetric difference then has zero geometric-mean mass to ordinary
successors:
$\sum_{s'\in\mathcal S^{(l-1)}}\widetilde T^{(l)}(s_i,s')=0$.
If alive states have no cemetery leakage, as for the stated nondegenerate
Stopping-Game kernel, its full geometric-mean row is also zero.

label: rem:adf-cemetery-floor
statement_tex:
[Cemetery floor]\label{rem:adf-cemetery-floor}
Theorem~\ref{thm:rand-adf} bounds only the ordinary-state overlap.  Overlap mass that reaches a
neuron dead in both models enters the cemetery in both, $g^{(l-1)}(\dagger) = g^{(l)}(\dagger) +
    \sum_{s \in \mathrm{dead}^{(l)}_A \cap \mathrm{dead}^{(l)}_B} g^{(l)}(s)$, and is never thinned
again, so plain $\mathrm{H}$ saturates below one.  In a mean-field approximation with uniform dead
fraction $q$ under $A$ and alive probability $p$ under $B$, the ordinary overlap shrinks by
$(1-q)p$ per layer while a fraction $q(1-p)$ is absorbed, so $g^{(0)}(\dagger) \to
    q(1-p)/(1-(1-q)p)$ as $N \to \infty$; for illustrative values $q = 0.2$, $p = \tfrac{1}{2}$ this
gives $\mathrm{H} \approx 0.91$, the same order as the observed $\drFloorMin$--$\drFloorMax$
(Table~\ref{tab:double-random-hellinger}).  The conditioned-survival distance removes the cemetery
floor exactly, and $\mathbb{E}_B[\mathrm{H}^2_{\mathrm{surv}} \mid Z_A Z_B \geq z] \to 1$ for every
fixed $z > 0$ with $\mathbb{P}_B(Z_A Z_B \geq z)$ bounded away from zero.  For the Routing Game the
activation-weighted kernel concentrates $g^{(l)}$ on neurons with largest $|a W|$, which rarely
coincide with $\mathrm{dead}_A \cap \mathrm{dead}_B$, so $\mathrm{H}$ is nearly identical to
$\mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{surv}}$ in practice.

statement_tex:
[Randomization in the Routing Game]\label{thm:rand-routing}

$\sum_{s'}\widetilde{T}^{(l)}(s, s') \leq \bar{b}$ for some $0 \leq \bar{b} < 1$.  Then
$\mathrm{BC}^{(0)}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\Pi_A, \Pi_B) \leq \bar{b}^{N}$.

rem:pair_notation
statement_tex:
[Pair notation for decomposed activations]\label{rem:pair_notation}
Superscript sign labels on \emph{activations}, written $\act{l}{\sigma}$ for $\sigma \in \{+,-\}$, are reserved for the two non-negative \emph{streams} of a network decomposition and are defined in Section~\ref{sec:general_decomposition_def}; they do \emph{not} denote the entrywise parts $\posneg{\actl{l}}{\sigma}$ of the original activations. The distinction matters: the decomposed streams carry strictly more information than the sign pattern of $\actl{l}$---the source of the sub-threshold signals exploited in Chapter~\ref{ch:saliency}.

label: def:cpwl
statement_tex:
[\ac{cpwl} function]\label{def:cpwl}
A function $f \colon \RR^{d} \to \RR^{m}$ is \emph{\acl{cpwl}} (\acs{cpwl}) if it is continuous and there exist finitely many closed polyhedra $Q_1, \ldots, Q_N \subseteq \RR^d$ with $\bigcup_{r=1}^{N} Q_r = \RR^d$ such that the restriction of $f$ to each $Q_r$ is an affine map. The full-dimensional polyhedra on which $f$ is affine, taken maximal with respect to inclusion, are called the \emph{linear regions} of $f$.

label: obs:relu_is_cpwl
statement_tex:
[\LeanResult{obs:relu_is_cpwl}]\label{obs:relu_is_cpwl}
Every feedforward \ac{relu} network represents a \ac{cpwl} function.
scope: Arbitrary signed weights, biases, varying widths and depth imply continuity and a genuine finite closed-polyhedral affine cover. Affine readout included where stated. This is not the arbitrary-CPWL network converse.

label: thm:cpwl_relu_equivalence
statement_tex:
[\ac{cpwl}--\ac{relu} equivalence, \parencite{Arora2018}, \LeanResult{thm:cpwl_relu_equivalence}]\label{thm:cpwl_relu_equivalence}
A function $f \colon \RR^{d} \to \RR$ is \ac{cpwl} if and only if it is representable by a feedforward \ac{relu} network. Moreover, every \ac{cpwl} function on $\RR^d$ is representable by a \ac{relu} network of depth at most $\bigl\lceil \log_2(d+1) \bigr\rceil + 1$.
scope: Both directions for genuine continuous finite-polyhedral-cover scalar CPWL functions on R^d, with explicit shared Network and signed affine readout witnesses; exact ceil(log_2(d+1))+1 total-layer bound. Includes arbitrary biases, nonconvex functions, d=0 and negative constants. Lattice/DC/signed-max/compiler bridges derived rather than assumed.

label: rem:linear_regions
statement_tex:
[Expressivity and linear regions]\label{rem:linear_regions}
Theorem~\ref{thm:cpwl_relu_equivalence} identifies the function \emph{class}, not the \emph{cost} of representation: deep networks can represent \ac{cpwl} functions with exponentially many linear regions in the number of neurons, an interplay of depth, width, and region counts surveyed by \textcite{huchette2025deeplearningmeetspolyhedral}. The tropical reformulation by \textcite{Zhang2018}---\ac{relu} networks as tropical rational maps---is taken up in Sections~\ref{sec:tropical_polyhedra_foundations} and \ref{sec:tropical_rational_maps}. The representation \eqref{eq:cpwl_dc_representation} also foreshadows the central theme of this thesis: the convex \ac{cpwl} streams $g$ and $h$ of the DC split can be extracted \emph{constructively and locally} from a trained network, the subject of Section~\ref{sec:dc_splitting_relu}.

label: def:monotone_network
statement_tex:
[Monotone neural network]\label{def:monotone_network}
A feedforward network with recursion \eqref{eq:forward_recursion} and monotone activation functions is called a \emph{monotone neural network} if all its weight matrices are entrywise non-negative, $\Wl{l} \ge 0$ for all $l = 1, \ldots, L$.

label: prop:monotone_represents
statement_tex:
[Monotone networks represent monotone functions, \LeanResult{prop:monotone_represents}]\label{prop:monotone_represents}
A monotone neural network represents a monotone function; each coordinate function is non-decreasing in every input variable.
scope: Arbitrary monotone scalar activation, shared varying-width network with nonnegative signed hidden weights, and actual nonnegative ungated affine readout.

label: def:icnn
statement_tex:
[\acl{icnn}, \parencite{Amos2017}]\label{def:icnn}
A feedforward network with recursion \eqref{eq:forward_recursion} whose activation functions are convex \emph{and} monotone is called an \emph{\acl{icnn}} (\acs{icnn}) if all weight matrices except possibly the first are entrywise non-negative, $\Wl{l} \ge 0$ for all $l = 2, \ldots, L$, while $\Wl{1}$ is unconstrained.

label: prop:icnn_convex
statement_tex:
[\acp{icnn} represent convex functions, \LeanResult{prop:icnn_convex}]\label{prop:icnn_convex}
An \ac{icnn} represents a convex function; each coordinate of every activation $\actl{l}$, $l \ge 1$, is a convex function of the input $x$.
scope: Coordinatewise genuine ConvexOn for arbitrary convex monotone scalar activation, unrestricted first affine weights, nonnegative later signed weights and actual nonnegative affine readout.

label: rem:monotone_convex_combined
statement_tex:
[Monotonicity and convexity combine]\label{rem:monotone_convex_combined}
If, in addition, $\Wl{1} \ge 0$ in Definition~\ref{def:icnn}, the network is simultaneously monotone and input-convex, hence non-decreasing \emph{and} convex by Propositions~\ref{prop:monotone_represents} and \ref{prop:icnn_convex}. Both $\relu$ and Maxout (below) are convex and monotone, so non-negative-weight \ac{relu} networks are of exactly this type. These are the building blocks of the DC splitting of Section~\ref{sec:dc_splitting_relu}: the streams $g$ and $h$ are computed by monotone networks acting on a signed embedding of the input, and are input-convex in the original input. The sign constraint also \emph{limits} expressivity---a weight-constrained \ac{relu} network represents only convex functions, precisely Proposition~\ref{prop:icnn_convex}, which is why monotone architectures add concave counterparts of the activation \parencite{Runje_2023}. The decompositions of this thesis turn the limitation into a feature: the difference of two such networks recovers full generality by Theorem~\ref{thm:cpwl_relu_equivalence} and \eqref{eq:cpwl_dc_representation}.

label: def:maxout
obs:relu_maxout_special_case
statement_tex:
[\ac{relu} and max-pooling as Maxout, \LeanResult{obs:relu_maxout_special_case}]\label{obs:relu_maxout_special_case}
The \ac{relu} activation is the rank-$2$ Maxout unit with parameters $(w_1, \beta_1) = (w, \beta)$ and $(w_2, \beta_2) = (0, 0)$, since $\relu(w^\top x + \beta) = \max\{w^\top x + \beta,\, 0\}$. Max-pooling over a group $J$ of neurons is the rank-$\abs{J}$ Maxout unit whose $j$-th argument is the coordinate projection onto the $j$-th element of $J$. Every rank-$k$ Maxout unit is convex in its input and non-decreasing in each pre-activation argument $w_j^\top x + \beta_j$; hence Maxout qualifies as an admissible activation in Definitions~\ref{def:monotone_network} and \ref{def:icnn}.
scope: Exact ReLU-as-two-piece-max and coordinate pooling, polynomial convexity and finite-maximum monotonicity; explicit finite nonempty index assumptions.

label: rem:maxout_role
statement_tex:
\label{rem:maxout_role}
Maxout networks are the natural piecewise-linear generalization of \ac{relu}: a rank-$k$ unit expresses a maximum of $k$ affine functions in one neuron, matching the building blocks of the DC representation \eqref{eq:cpwl_dc_representation}. The DC splitting of Chapter~\ref{ch:decompositions} is developed for \ac{relu} networks and extended to Maxout units---and to the multiplicative interactions needed for attention---in Chapter~\ref{ch:transformers}, using the exchange identity $\max_{j \in [k]}(u_j - v_j) = \max_{j \in [k]}\bigl\{ u_j + \sum_{i \ne j} v_i \bigr\} - \sum_{i \in [k]} v_i$ for pairs of non-negative streams.

label: rem:structural_discount
def:turn_based_game
statement_tex:
[Zero-sum turn-based game]\label{def:turn_based_game}
A (finite) \emph{zero-sum turn-based game} is a tuple $\mathcal{G} = (S_{+}, S_{-}, S_{\mathrm{ter}}, A, \P, R, \gamma)$ where the state set $S = S_{+} \uplus S_{-} \uplus S_{\mathrm{ter}}$ is partitioned into states controlled by player $P^{+}$, states controlled by player $P^{-}$, and terminal states; the action sets $A(s)$, the transition kernel $\P$, and the reward $R$ are as in Definition~\ref{def:mdp} on non-terminal states; $\gamma \colon S \to \RR_{\ge 0}$ is a (possibly state-dependent) discount; and each terminal state $s \in S_{\mathrm{ter}}$ carries a fixed one-time payoff $R(s)$. A \emph{policy pair} $\pi = (\pi_{+}, \pi_{-})$ consists of a policy $\pi_{p}$ for player $P^{p}$ on $S_{p}$. Play generates a trajectory as in an \ac{mdp}, with the player in turn choosing the action; the expected total payoff $V^{\pi}(s)$, defined as in \eqref{eq:mdp_value} with the discount accumulated multiplicatively along the trajectory ($\gamma^t$ replaced by $\prod_{m=0}^{t-1}\gamma(s_m)$), is paid \emph{by $P^{-}$ to $P^{+}$}: player $P^{+}$ maximizes $V^{\pi}$ and player $P^{-}$ minimizes it.

label: rem:shapley_history
statement_tex:
\label{rem:shapley_history}
For general discounted stochastic games with cycles, existence of the value and of optimal stationary policies is Shapley's theorem \parencite{Shapley1953stochastic}, proved by the contraction argument of Proposition~\ref{prop:bellman} applied to the \emph{Shapley operator}---the min-max analogue of the Bellman operator \eqref{eq:shapley_bellman}. \textcite{Gaubert2025} formulate their network games in this operator language. The layered acyclic case of Theorem~\ref{thm:shapley_bellman} is all we need, and it additionally delivers subgame perfection, on which Chapter~\ref{ch:trajectory} relies.

label: def:relu_net_game
thm:relu_net_game_value
scope: Actual normalized ReLU game with nonzero fan-in and forced ungated affine output: saddle against all randomized profiles, exact selected payoff, exact all-subgame iff tie-permitted 0/1 gate conditions, and same output payoff for every subgame-perfect profile. Direct recursive all-state randomized best-response predicate on Strategy iff both players continue with probability one at strictly positive preactivations and zero at strictly negative ones; arbitrary probabilities permitted at ties.

rem:inherited_vs_new
statement_tex:
[What Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} inherits and what it changes]\label{rem:inherited_vs_new}
The \ac{sg} of Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} keeps the structural skeleton of Definition~\ref{def:relu_net_game}: per-neuron $\pm$ states, stop-versus-continue actions, the bias as continuation payoff and the input as final payoff, the transition kernel \eqref{eq:rng_kernel} driven by the weight parts $\Wsig{l}{\sigma}$, the cemetery state, and the structural discounts $\gamma^{(l)}_i$. Two changes are load-bearing for attribution. First, the original tracks only the single signed value \eqref{eq:rng_value_identity}; Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} additionally maintains a \emph{non-negative payoff per player}, identifying the pair of player-specific values $\Vp{p}{s}$, $p \in \{+,-\}$, with the two streams of the Stopping Decomposition of Section~\ref{sec:stopping_decomposition} and recovering \eqref{eq:rng_value_identity} as their difference. Second, the signed terminal payoffs $\xi_q\, x_k$ become the non-negative pair $(x_k^{+}, x_k^{-})$ of Definition~\ref{def:posneg_parts}, keeping every player-specific quantity non-negative and exposing the parity structure of backward trajectories. Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} further extends the graph to skip connections and max-pooling and adds risk aversion and regularized policies, none of which appear in the original game.

def:tropical_polynomial
obs:tropical_convex_cpwl
statement_tex:
[Tropical polynomials are the convex \ac{cpwl} functions, \LeanResult{obs:tropical_convex_cpwl}]\label{obs:tropical_convex_cpwl}
A function $p \colon \RR^d \to \RR$ is a tropical polynomial \eqref{eq:tropical_polynomial} if and only if it is convex and \ac{cpwl}.
scope: Exact scalar convex CPWL iff finite max-affine representation, derived from the genuine finite closed-polyhedral cover by dense interiors and convex local-to-global minima; no representation assumption or substitute CPWL definition.

label: def:newton_polytope
def:minkowski_sum
statement_tex:
[Minkowski sum]\label{def:minkowski_sum}
The \emph{Minkowski sum} of two sets $P, Q \subseteq \RR^{d}$ is $P + Q \coloneqq \{ u + v : u \in P,\, v \in Q \}$. For polytopes $P$ and $Q$ the Minkowski sum is again a polytope, and every vertex of $P + Q$ decomposes as the sum of a vertex of $P$ and a vertex of $Q$ \parencite{Ziegler1995}.

label: def:support_function
lem:support_properties
scope: Full nonempty compact-convex support calculus; arbitrary compact convex sets for convexity, homogeneity, sums/unions, containment and uniqueness; separate nonempty finite hull formula and extreme-point attainment.

label: prop:newton_calculus
scope: Actual Newton sets under tropical addition/maximum, exact function identities, homogenized slice support and zero-intercept unlifted support.

label: rem:polytope_layer_transitions
statement_tex:
[Layer transitions as polytope operations]\label{rem:polytope_layer_transitions}
Proposition~\ref{prop:newton_calculus} is the dictionary used in the remaining subsections: an affine layer with non-negative weights acts on the tropical polynomials computed by the previous layer through tropical products and powers---Minkowski sums and scalings of Newton polytopes---while $\relu$ and Maxout gates act through tropical sums---convex hulls of unions. The convex streams $g$ and $h$ of the DC decomposition---developed in full in Chapter~\ref{ch:decompositions}---are, by Observation~\ref{obs:tropical_convex_cpwl}, tropical polynomials, so their (lifted) Newton polytopes are computable layer by layer. Section~\ref{sec:imaginative_polytopes} studies these polytopes: by Lemma~\ref{lem:support_properties}.3 they encode the split streams faithfully, and their vertices are exactly the attainable gradients of $g$ and $h$---the geometric objects behind the \emph{imaginative polytopes} of this thesis. For the broader landscape connecting polyhedral and tropical geometry with network expressivity, see \parencite{Zhang2018,Brandenburg2024b,huchette2025deeplearningmeetspolyhedral}.

label: thm:split_tropical_rational
scope: Bias-free hidden network and ungated signed affine readout: constructed heads have zero intercepts, nonnegative slopes, monotonicity, convexity, positive homogeneity; exact actual split affine-head evaluations, exact signed logit difference and final weighted Minkowski sets. Includes zero hidden layers.

label: thm:monotone_nonneg_gradients
statement_tex:
[Monotone \ac{cpwl} functions have non-negative gradients, \LeanResult{thm:monotone_nonneg_gradients}]\label{thm:monotone_nonneg_gradients}
Let $u \colon \RR^n \to \RR$ be monotone and \ac{cpwl}. Then every gradient attained by $u$ at a point of differentiability is entrywise non-negative.
scope: Nonnegative directional derivative at differentiable points; no subdifferential theorem.

label: cor:minkowski_propagation
statement_tex:
[Minkowski-sum propagation across layers, \LeanResult{cor:minkowski_propagation}]\label{cor:minkowski_propagation}
For a bias-free \ac{relu} \ac{mlp} with split streams \eqref{eq:split_preact_recursion}--\eqref{eq:split_act_recursion}, the Newton polytopes of the split activations satisfy
\begin{align}
    P^{(0,+)}_j &= \{ e_j \},
    \qquad
    P^{(0,-)}_j = \{ e_{d+j} \},
    \qquad j \in [d], \notag \\
    Q^{(l,+)}_i &\coloneqq \bigoplus_j \Bigl( \Wsig{l}{+}_{ij} P^{(l-1,+)}_j \oplus \Wsig{l}{-}_{ij} P^{(l-1,-)}_j \Bigr),
    \quad
    Q^{(l,-)}_i \coloneqq \bigoplus_j \Bigl( \Wsig{l}{-}_{ij} P^{(l-1,+)}_j \oplus \Wsig{l}{+}_{ij} P^{(l-1,-)}_j \Bigr),
    \label{eq:polytope_preact} \\
    P^{(l,+)}_i &= \operatorname{conv}\Bigl( Q^{(l,+)}_i \cup Q^{(l,-)}_i \Bigr),
    \qquad
    P^{(l,-)}_i = Q^{(l,-)}_i,
    \label{eq:polytope_act}
\end{align}
where the activation update~\eqref{eq:polytope_act} applies only to $l<L$; at the affine readout set $P^{(L,\pm)}_i=Q^{(L,\pm)}_i$. Here $e_1, \dots, e_{2d}$ are the standard basis of $\RR^{2d}$ and $\oplus$ the Minkowski sum. The Newton polytopes $P_g \coloneqq \operatorname{Newt}(g)$ and $P_h \coloneqq \operatorname{Newt}(h)$ of a scalar output neuron are obtained after $L$ steps.
scope: Actual basis-singleton initial sets, every hidden weighted Minkowski/hull propagation, and both ungated signed affine output sums, including arbitrary stored biases and zero hidden layers.

label: prop:subdifferential_face
statement_tex:
[Subdifferential of a support function, \LeanResult{prop:subdifferential_face}]\label{prop:subdifferential_face}
Let $P \subseteq \RR^n$ be a polytope and $x \in \RR^n$. Then $\partial h_P(x) = F_P(x) = \{ p \in P : \langle p, x \rangle = h_P(x) \}$, the maximizing face. In particular, $h_P$ is differentiable at $x$ if and only if $F_P(x)$ is a singleton, in which case $\nabla h_P(x) \in P$.
scope: Nonempty finite-hull support: actual subgradient inequality iff maximizing face, genuine Frechet differentiability iff singleton exposed face, and every attained gradient lies in the hull.

label: def:imaginative_polytopes
statement_tex:
[Imaginative Polytopes]\label{def:imaginative_polytopes}
Let $g, h \colon \RR^{2d} \to \RR$ be the split streams of an output neuron of a bias-free \ac{relu} network. The \emph{Imaginative Polytopes} of that neuron are the Newton polytopes $P_g \coloneqq \operatorname{Newt}(g)$ and $P_h \coloneqq \operatorname{Newt}(h)$, i.e.\ the unique polytopes in $\RR^{2d}$ whose support functions are $g$ and $h$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:support_properties}).

label: cor:polytopes_nonneg
statement_tex:
[Imaginative Polytopes live in the non-negative orthant, \LeanResult{cor:polytopes_nonneg}]\label{cor:polytopes_nonneg}
$P_g, P_h \subseteq \RR^{2d}_{\ge 0}$.
scope: Both actual Newton convex hulls of constructively propagated network split polynomials are contained in the nonnegative orthant.

label: thm:vertices_gradients
scope: Arbitrary positively homogeneous convex CPWL function: existence and uniqueness of its nonempty Newton polytope and exact equality of its extreme points with all genuine Frechet gradient vectors. Generic finite lifted hull: actual derivatives after restriction to (x,1) exactly project slice-visible uniquely exposed lifted vertices.

label: def:decomposition
def:valid_decomposition
prop:validity_recovery
scope: Full varying-width shared network with arbitrary scalar and pair activations and biases. Scalar difference preservation implies full network recovery; nonnegative pair output is proved separately under explicit nonnegative parameter/input/activation assumptions.

label: prop:dc_profile_lift
scope: Exact global convexity iff, derivative-free increment iff, differentiable slope iff, and valid paired lift for arbitrary real profiles, including nonsmooth ReLU. The generic origin-normalization iff in the final sentence is not a selected Lean contract; nonnegative-quadrant preservation is separately proved for the constructed curvature and explicit activation pairs.

label: thm:general_dc_network
scope: Actual finite varying-width backbone with a shared scalar activation and genuine ungated signed affine readout: jointly convex monotone heads and exact recovery for all real pair inputs. Split-weight positivity suffices for these properties; nonnegative split biases and input streams additionally give nonnegative values through the separate network and affine-chunk results. Arbitrary convex input substitution is covered by the composition lemma, with the usual positive/negative split explicitly instantiated. Every suffix is an admissible network; no heterogeneous per-layer activation API is asserted.

label: thm:absolute_curvature_split
scope: Constructive global convex monotone exact pair from the actual positive and negative curvature integrals, under differentiability, locally absolutely continuous derivative, and integrable actual curvature; common normalization handles arbitrary f(0), with nonnegative values on the input quadrant. Lean uses C1/C2 plus the shared slope shift and constant offset. This is algebraically equivalent to the displayed D-based profiles, but no Lean equality bridge to that D formula, positive-infinity slope limit, displayed absolute-value coefficient formula, or coefficient-optimality claim is included.

label: rem:global_curvature_necessity
scope: The global necessity argument for arbitrary finite convex coordinatewise monotone bivariate pairs is given analytically in the text. No Lean bounded-variation or curvature-measure necessity theorem is claimed; the formal profile iff only characterizes the specified affine-lift ansatz.

label: cor:local_curvature_split
statement_tex:
[Exact splitting on a bounded activation interval]\label{cor:local_curvature_split}
Let $a<b$ and let $f\in C^1([a,b])$ have absolutely continuous derivative. There exist finite-valued convex, coordinatewise non-decreasing functions $F_+,F_-\colon\RR^2\to\RR$, non-negative on $\RR^2_{\ge0}$, such that $F_+(x,y)-F_-(x,y)=f(x-y)$ whenever $x-y\in[a,b]$.
scope: The bounded-interval tangent-extension argument is proved in the manuscript. No Lean construction and gluing theorem for this extension has been integrated.

label: prop:stream_properties
statement_tex:
[Monotonicity and convexity of the split streams, \LeanResult{prop:stream_properties}]\label{prop:stream_properties}
For every $0 \le l \le L$, the stream functions $g^{(l)}$ and $h^{(l)}$ of~\eqref{eq:stream_functions} are convex and non-decreasing in each coordinate of the pair $(x^+, x^-) \in \RR^{d^{(l)}} \times \RR^{d^{(l)}}$.
scope: Instantiate the generic actual-network construction at the literal ReLU max/identity pair. Both heads, including an ungated signed affine readout, are globally jointly convex and coordinatewise monotone in the independent doubled inputs. Split biases are unrestricted and widths may be zero; every tail is an admissible network and the terminal tail is identity.

label: thm:split_correct
scope: Actual shared varying-width MLP backbone plus an arbitrary ungated signed affine readout with split biases; difference recovery for both real input streams. The generic backbone identity is also retained.

label: rem:subthreshold
statement_tex:
[Preservation of sub-threshold signals]\label{rem:subthreshold}
The correctness theorem hides an information-theoretic asymmetry between the original and the split network. When a neuron is inactive, $\preactl{l}_i \le 0$, the original \ac{relu} outputs $\actl{l}_i = 0$ and discards the \emph{magnitude} of the losing pre-activation: downstream computation is oblivious to how strongly the neuron was suppressed. The split pair reads $\bigl(\act{l}{+}_i, \act{l}{-}_i\bigr) = \bigl(\preact{l}{-}_i, \preact{l}{-}_i\bigr)$: the difference is zero, as validity demands, but both components retain the accumulated magnitude $\preact{l}{-}_i$ of the cancelled mass and propagate it forward. The split streams thus carry strictly more information than the original activations---sub-threshold contributions survive the gate---which the attribution methods of Chapter~\ref{ch:saliency} exploit. The same effect drives the numerical growth of Section~\ref{sec:stabilization_dc}: without cancellation by subtraction, both streams accumulate the absolute mass $\preact{l}{+}_i + \preact{l}{-}_i$ instead of the signed residual.

label: rem:input_split_flexibility
statement_tex:
[Flexibility of the input split]\label{rem:input_split_flexibility}
Theorem~\ref{thm:split_correct} holds for \emph{any} non-negative representation $x = x^+ - x^-$: the entrywise split $x^\pm = \posneg{x}{\pm}$ or the symmetric split $x^\pm = \posneg{x}{\pm} + c$ with $c \ge 0$. This degree of freedom is exploited both for numerical stabilization and for the baseline choices of the attribution methods in Chapter~\ref{ch:saliency}. The half--half split $x^\pm = \pm x/2$ of Section~\ref{sec:stabilization_dc} is \emph{not} such a non-negative input split---its negative component is signed---but a chain-rule device for the backward pass, used only to differentiate the split streams along the unified input direction.

label: cor:closed_form_dc_activations
statement_tex:
[Explicit convex, monotone activation pairs, \LeanResult{cor:closed_form_dc_activations}]\label{cor:closed_form_dc_activations}
For $f(z)=z\Phi(z)$ (GELU), $f(z)=z\sigma(\beta z)$ (Swish), $f=\sigma$ (sigmoid), and $f=s_{1/\theta}$ (softplus), choose the corresponding row of Table~\ref{tab:closed_form_dc_profiles}. Then the functions $F_+(x,y)=p(x-y)+Ly$ and $F_-(x,y)=q(x-y)+Ly$ are convex and coordinatewise non-decreasing on $\RR^2$, map $\RR^2_{\ge0}$ to itself, and satisfy $F_+-F_-=f(x-y)$.
scope: The actual root-free table profiles for exact Gaussian GELU, positive-scale Swish, smooth sigmoid, and positive-temperature Softplus give globally convex coordinatewise monotone pairs, exact recovery, and nonnegative-quadrant preservation. The root-free formulas are distinct from the curvature-minimal profiles; no equality between these constructions is asserted.

label: cor:modern_activations
statement_tex:
[Modern activation functions, \LeanResult{cor:modern_activations}]\label{cor:modern_activations}
Theorems~\ref{thm:absolute_curvature_split} and~\ref{thm:smooth_dc_split} apply to the following activation functions, where $\varphi$ and $\Phi$ denote the standard Gaussian density and distribution function and $\sigma(x) = (1+e^{-x})^{-1}$ the logistic sigmoid:
\begin{enumerate}
	\item \emph{GELU}, $f(x) = x\,\Phi(x)$, with $f''(x) = (2 - x^2)\,\varphi(x)$; the curvature is positive on $(-\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{2})$ and negative outside.
	\item \emph{Swish/SiLU}, $f(x) = x\,\sigma(\beta x)$ with $\beta > 0$, with $f''(x) = \beta\,\sigma'(\beta x)\bigl( 2 + \beta x\,(1 - 2\sigma(\beta x)) \bigr)$; the curvature is positive on a bounded interval around the origin and negative in both tails.
	\item \emph{Mish}, $f(x) = x \tanh\bigl(\log(1 + e^{x})\bigr)$.
	\item \emph{Hyperbolic tangent}, $f(x) = \tanh(x)$, with $f''(x) = -2 \tanh(x)\operatorname{sech}^2(x)$, so $P$ is supported on $(-\infty, 0]$ and $N$ on $[0, \infty)$.
	\item \emph{Logistic sigmoid}, $f = \sigma$, with $f'' = \sigma'\,(1 - 2\sigma)$.
	\item \emph{Softplus at temperature $\theta > 0$}, $f(x) = \theta \log(1 + e^{x/\theta})$, with $f''(x) = \sigma'(x/\theta)/\theta \ge 0$; here $N = 0$, $C_2 = 0$, and the decomposition degenerates to the statement that softplus itself is convex.
\end{enumerate}
In each case $f(0) \ge 0$, and both constructions preserve non-negativity on the input quadrant (Remark~\ref{rem:smooth_valid_decomposition}).
scope: All six literal activations: exact Gaussian GELU, positive-scale Swish, Mish, tanh, sigmoid, and positive-temperature Softplus. The existing complete theorem proves analytic regularity, actual curvature formulas/sign cases, symmetric-tilt validity, and nonnegative-quadrant preservation; the additional asymmetric integral-curvature pair theorem proves the corresponding convex, monotone, valid, nonnegative pair. No global routing-game interpretation of signed activations is asserted.

label: cor:smooth_dc_networks
statement_tex:
[Networks with smooth activations, \LeanResult{cor:smooth_dc_networks}]\label{cor:smooth_dc_networks}
Every finite feedforward network with GELU, Swish/SiLU, sigmoid, or softplus hidden activations, arbitrary signed weights and biases, and an affine output admits an exact decomposition into two convex, coordinatewise non-decreasing streams on doubled input space. Either the explicit profiles of Corollary~\ref{cor:closed_form_dc_activations} or the canonical profiles~\eqref{eq:sigmoid_canonical_dc}--\eqref{eq:gelu_swish_canonical_dc} and~\eqref{eq:softplus_dc_closed} may be used at every hidden neuron. With the usual non-negative input split, the streams remain non-negative and their pullbacks are convex functions of the original signed input. The same existence result holds for Mish and tanh by Theorem~\ref{thm:absolute_curvature_split}.
scope: Complete same-parameter finite networks with a shared requested activation and ungated signed affine readout, using the actual root-free pairs or the integral-curvature pairs; the latter also cover Mish and tanh. Convexity and monotonicity hold on doubled inputs, while the standard signed input split preserves convexity and exact recovery. Nonnegative values use canonical nonnegative split biases and input streams, with the final affine chunk covered separately. No formal equality to every displayed canonical piecewise formula, and no heterogeneous per-layer activation interface, is claimed.

label: rem:smooth_pointer
statement_tex:
[Scope of the smooth extension]\label{rem:smooth_pointer}
The extension above is an exact structural theorem about the scalar activations and their composition into feedforward networks. It does not establish empirical attribution quality for these smooth networks, nor does it by itself extend the ReLU-specific tropical polytope representation, hard-gate games, or numerical stabilization formulas. The experiments later in the thesis evaluate the architectures and methods described in their protocols; the new smooth formulas are not additional experimental results.

label: prop:multivariate_dc_lift
scope: The formal helper covers the uniform-coefficient lift P(x-y)+L*sum(y)-c: sufficient convexity, sufficient monotonicity from monotonicity of P and L*sum-P, exact difference, and nonnegative-orthant preservation under c<=P(0). The source proposition additionally allows an arbitrary coefficient vector and states converse convexity/derivative-bound equivalences; those general clauses are not formalized by this leaf. The specialized softmax result is independently proved without these missing general converses.

label: thm:softmax_dc_split
scope: The literal normalized log-sum-exp plus/minus softmax heads for every finite nonempty index type and every output coordinate: global joint convexity and coordinatewise monotonicity on independent real stream vectors, exact recovery, and nonnegative values on the expanded nonnegative orthant. The normalizer is exactly (log(n)-1/n)/2, with origin values 1/n and 0. Singleton rows are included; empty rows are excluded. Actual softmax derivatives and curvature bounds are proved, not assumed. This is a row primitive, not a complete masked-attention or Transformer compilation theorem.

label: thm:smooth_dc_split
scope: Actual curvature integrals, local absolute continuity of the derivative, globally integrable curvature, convex monotone primitive pair and exact reconstruction.

label: prop:curvature_minimality
statement_tex:
[Minimality of the curvature split, \LeanResult{prop:curvature_minimality}]\label{prop:curvature_minimality}
Let $f$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:smooth_dc_split} and suppose $f = c_1 - c_2$ for convex functions $c_1, c_2 \colon \RR \to \RR$ whose second distributional derivatives are locally integrable functions. Then $c_1'' \ge P$ and $c_2'' \ge N$ almost everywhere. In particular, $(C_1, C_2)$ is, up to a common affine summand, the unique pair of convex functions with $C_1 - C_2 = f$ of pointwise minimal curvature, and among all tilts of the form $(a,b) \mapsto \lambda(a+b)$, $\lambda \ge 0$, the constant $M$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:smooth_dc_split} is the smallest one rendering both components of \eqref{eq:smooth_split_pair} non-decreasing in each argument.
scope: Actual locally integrable distributional second derivatives defined by compactly supported smooth test functions. Convexity supplies continuity; differentiability/local absolute continuity are derived. Both curvature bounds, common-affine uniqueness and least tilt follow without assuming the desired classical regularity.

label: rem:bv_extension
statement_tex:
[Bounded variation and the piecewise-linear case]\label{rem:bv_extension}
The curvature construction extends to locally absolutely continuous $f$ whose weak derivative has a bounded-variation representative: its distributional second derivative is a finite signed Radon measure $\mu$. Replacing $|f''(u)|\,\diff u$ by $|\mu|$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:absolute_curvature_split}, or replacing $P(u)\,\diff u$ and $N(u)\,\diff u$ by the Jordan parts $\mu_+,\mu_-$, gives convex profiles with bounded slopes; the increment criterion~\eqref{eq:dc_profile_increments} replaces pointwise derivative conditions at kinks. For ReLU, $\mu=\delta_0$, $s_-=0$, and the canonical profiles are $p(z)=\max\{z,0\}$, $q=0$, $L=1$. Thus the asymmetric lift gives exactly $(\max\{a,b\},b)$, not merely a pair with the same difference. The symmetric variant instead gives $(\relu(a-b)+a+b,a+b)$. Leaky ReLU with slope $\alpha$ has curvature measure $(1-\alpha)\delta_0$; the standard ELU with unit negative-branch scale has curvature $e^z\indicator{z<0}\,\diff z$. Both fit the finite-measure construction. Piecewise-linear and smooth activations are therefore covered by the same curvature principle, with differentiability replaced by bounded variation where needed.

label: rem:smooth_valid_decomposition
statement_tex:
[Compatibility with valid decompositions]\label{rem:smooth_valid_decomposition}
Both constructions fit Definition~\ref{def:decomposition}. For the canonical asymmetric pair, $F_+(0,0)=\max\{f(0),0\}$ and $F_-(0,0)=\max\{-f(0),0\}$ are non-negative; coordinatewise monotonicity then ensures non-negative values throughout $\RR^2_{\ge0}$. For the symmetric pair~\eqref{eq:smooth_split_pair}, the origin values are $g(0,0)=f(0)$ and $h(0,0)=0$, so the same argument applies whenever $f(0)\ge0$, as for every activation in Corollary~\ref{cor:modern_activations}. If $f(0)<0$, adding $|f(0)|$ to both symmetric components restores non-negativity without affecting their difference. Exactness is precisely the activation-level validity condition; Theorem~\ref{thm:general_dc_network} supplies network recovery, convexity, and monotonicity.

label: def:fmix
thm:mixing_recovery
scope: Full varying-width network eta-mixing recovery for every real eta; nonnegative streams when eta is in [0,1] and parameters/input pairs are nonnegative.

label: thm:mixing_convex_extreme
scope: Arbitrary coordinatewise convex input lifts, actual nonnegative split network, arbitrary biases and varying widths. Both mixing-one streams and actual ungated nonnegative affine heads are convex. Recovery is net.eval(p−q); the source input-split identity specializes this to the original input.

label: rem:eta_zero_extreme
statement_tex:
[On the $\eta = 0$ extreme]\label{rem:eta_zero_extreme}
The dual \ac{dc} representation writes the output as $u(x) - v(x)$ with $v$ \emph{concave}, and $\fmix[0]$ places $a_{\mathrm{mix},i}^{(l,-,0)} = \min\bigl\{\preact{l}{+}_i, \preact{l}{-}_i\bigr\}$ in the role of $v$. This is concave only when both decomposed pre-activations are concave (or affine): the minimum of two concave functions is concave, but of two convex functions is in general neither. Under the input convention~\eqref{eq:input_split_convention}, the first pre-activations are convex in $x$, but later $\eta=0$ streams and pre-activations need not remain convex or concave. A canonical scalar example is $W^{(1)}=1$, $b^{(1)}=1$, giving the negative stream $v(x)=\min\{\max(x,0)+1,\max(-x,0)\}$. It satisfies $v(-2)=v(-1)=1$, $v(0)=v(1)=0$: the midpoint tests at $-1$ and $0$ respectively exclude convexity and concavity. By Theorem~\ref{thm:mixing_recovery}, $\fmix[0]$ still yields a valid arithmetic decomposition, and the network-level concave representation is recoverable with an unsplit affine input convention, at the cost of the $\pm$ structure.

label: cor:dc_split_endpoint
statement_tex:
[DC split as the $\eta = 1$ mixing endpoint, \LeanResult{cor:dc_split_endpoint}]\label{cor:dc_split_endpoint}
Set $\eta = 1$ in Definition~\ref{def:fmix} and drop the decomposition tag, writing $\act{l}{\pm} \coloneqq a_{\mathrm{mix}}^{(l,\pm,1)}$. The resulting \emph{\ac{dc} split} applies the update~\eqref{eq:dc_split_activations} entrywise at hidden layers $l = 1, \dots, L-1$, and sets $\act{L}{\pm}=\preact{L}{\pm}$ at the final affine readout, with the decomposed pre-activations \eqref{eq:split_pos}--\eqref{eq:split_neg} induced by the weight split $\Wl{l} = \Wsig{l}{+} - \Wsig{l}{-}$ and the input split $x = x^+ - x^-$. It is a valid decomposition of the \ac{relu} network, and under the input convention of Theorem~\ref{thm:mixing_convex_extreme} its decomposed activations are convex functions of the input.
scope: Literal eta-one identity with the actual DC split, exact reconstruction, convexity under arbitrary convex input lifts, and actual final affine-head convexity/recovery.

label: def:fstop
thm:stopping_validity
scope: Actual shared varying-width Network stopping decomposition, exact difference recovery and nonnegative components. Ungated readout extension is separate.

label: rem:gate_vs_maxima
statement_tex:
[Shared gate versus per-stream maxima]\label{rem:gate_vs_maxima}
The contrast with the mixing family is sharpest at an inactive neuron, $\preactl{l}_i \le 0$. The \ac{dc} split of Corollary~\ref{cor:dc_split_endpoint} outputs $\bigl(\preact{l}{-}_i, \preact{l}{-}_i\bigr)$, preserving the sub-threshold magnitude (Remark~\ref{rem:subthreshold}) at the price of letting cancelled mass flow onward. The Stopping Decomposition outputs $(0, 0)$: the shared hard gate annihilates \emph{both} streams exactly where the original \ac{relu} annihilates its activation, so decomposed mass flows only along neurons active in the original network. The mixing streams are convex (at $\eta = 1$) but blend contributions of dead neurons into every downstream pair; the stopping streams sacrifice global convexity---the gate is discontinuous---for exact support agreement with the original forward pass, while remaining as well-behaved as possible on each linear region.

label: lem:stop_monotone
statement_tex:
[Monotonicity of the Stopping Decomposition on linear regions, \LeanResult{lem:stop_monotone}]\label{lem:stop_monotone}

label: rem:soft-monotone
statement_tex:
[Loss of stream monotonicity]\label{rem:soft-monotone}
The soft gate does not inherit the well-behavedness of the hard-gated Stopping Decomposition. Consider the negative stream $\act{l}{-} = \sigma'_\theta(\Delta)\, z^-$ with $\Delta = z^+ - z^-$: holding $z^+$ fixed and increasing $z^-$ both raises the factor $z^-$ and, through $\Delta$, \emph{lowers} the gate $\sigma'_\theta(\Delta)$. Differentiating, $\partial \act{l}{-} / \partial z^- = \sigma'_\theta(\Delta)\bigl(1 - z^-\, \sigma''_\theta(\Delta)/\sigma'_\theta(\Delta)\bigr)$ turns negative once $z^-$ exceeds $\theta / \bigl(1 - \sigma'_\theta(\Delta)\bigr)$, so $a_{\mathrm{soft}}^{(l,-)}$ is \emph{not} monotone non-decreasing in $z^-$. The per-region monotonicity of the Stopping Decomposition (Lemma~\ref{lem:stop_monotone}) therefore does not lift to the soft-gated family; the reader should not expect the Softplus Decomposition to inherit the monotone or convex structure of the hard-gated and \ac{dc} decompositions. Only the difference recovery of Theorem~\ref{thm:freg_validity} survives.

statement_tex:
[Connection to the integrable-curvature splitting]\label{rem:freg_smooth_connection}
Regularized gates connect to the convex activations covered by Theorem~\ref{thm:smooth_dc_split}. Suppose $\Omega$ is strictly convex and the gate $\pi_\Omega$ is locally absolutely continuous on $\RR$. Then $\Omega^*$ is differentiable with $(\Omega^*)' = \pi_\Omega$, which is non-decreasing with limits $0$ and $1$ at $-\infty$ and $+\infty$. Hence the weak curvature $(\Omega^*)'' \ge 0$ belongs to $L^1(\RR)$ and integrates to $1$. A sufficient condition is $\Omega\in C^2((0,1))$ with $\Omega''>0$ there: the gate is the inverse of $\Omega'$ on its range, extended by $0$ and $1$ beyond finite endpoint slopes. Strict convexity and smoothness alone do not guarantee local absolute continuity of the gate; the distributional curvature can have a singular part. Under the stated regularity, Theorem~\ref{thm:smooth_dc_split} applies with $N = 0$, $C_2 = 0$, and $C_1=\Omega^*$, as recorded for the softplus in Corollary~\ref{cor:modern_activations}(6). Regularizing the \emph{gate} (this section) and the curvature-based smooth split of Section~\ref{sec:dc_splitting_smooth} thus yield compatible valid decompositions of the same networks under these hypotheses, cf.\ Remark~\ref{rem:smooth_valid_decomposition}.

statement_tex:
[Interpretation of the correction terms]\label{rem:Q_network}
The correction summands in~\eqref{eq:closed_formula_g} are gradients of an auxiliary network: define $Q[j](x) \coloneqq W_{\mathrm{abs}}^{[j,\rightarrow]}\min\{\preactl{j}(x),0\}$, with the original prefix through layer $j$ followed by a linear absolute-weight tail without biases or activation gates. In a bias-free tail this agrees in value with subsequent minimum activations, but the explicit definition also handles arbitrary prefix biases. Then the $j$-th summand equals $\overline{\alpha}_{j+1}\, \partial Q[j+1] / \partial x$ (at $l = 0$), capturing the mass that switches streams at layer $j+1$. These gradients grow rapidly toward the input, so the factors $\overline{\alpha}_j$ act as a per-layer lever that both prevents gradient explosion and regulates how strongly each layer's stream-switching enters the stabilized gradients. In practice all $\alpha^{(l)}$ equal a common $\alpha$; for $\alpha = 1/2$ the sensitivities are exact halves of the original gradient, for $\alpha = 0$ the raw split-pair gradients, and $0 < \alpha < 1/2$ is the interesting regime. These stabilized gradients are the backbone of the split saliency methods in Chapter~\ref{ch:saliency}.

statement_tex:
[A probabilistic reading]\label{rem:splitlrp_markov}
On the original network the $\varepsilon$-rule mixes signed contributions, and the resulting backward transport is a \emph{signed} measure on paths --- the source of the interpretability caveats discussed in Chapter~\ref{ch:trajectory}. On the split-pair all contributions $\tilde{z}^{(l+1)}_{ij}$ are products of non-negative activations and non-negative weights, so up to the stabilizer the \ac{lrp} propagation matrices are genuinely stochastic: SplitLRP is a Markov chain on the doubled computational graph, and the pair $\bigl(R^{(l,+)}, R^{(l,-)}\bigr)$ is an honest, unsigned relevance measure. This is the same mechanism --- doubling the state space to absorb the weight signs --- by which the stopping game of Chapter~\ref{ch:game_theory} turns backward relevance flow into probability.

[Sensitivity to learned parameters]\label{rem:splitlrp_sanity}
The parameter-randomization sanity check of \textcite{Adebayo2018sanity} differentiates the three split methods. After reinitializing the last three feedforward layers of VGG-16, every reported SplitCAM and SplitGrad configuration has lower SSIM than every listed baseline, whereas the HOG and Spearman comparisons are mixed. This establishes sensitivity to the tested parameter changes, not faithfulness to the learned decision process. SplitLRP retains high HOG and Spearman similarity despite a decrease in SSIM. Attenuation by the $\varepsilon$-\ac{lrp} rule is a possible explanation, consistent with concerns about conservative propagation rules~\parencite{sixt2020whenexplanationslie}, but this comparison does not identify the mechanism. Section~\ref{app:p1_sanity} reports the quantitative results and the caveats of \textcite{Binder2022shortcomings} on randomization-based checks.

statement_tex:
[Post-hoc and by-design, reconciled]\label{rem:posthoc_bydesign}
The two routes of this chapter probe the same structural hypothesis --- that difference-of-monotone representations can make network sensitivities more legible --- from opposite ends. The MNIST study establishes that differences of constrained networks can be trained directly to competitive accuracy. Its visual examples also exhibit class-dependent stream sensitivities on present and candidate missing strokes. These qualitative observations do not establish faithful counterfactual explanations or a general separation of explanatory roles, either for the trained models or for the split-pairs of the pretrained VGG-16 and ResNet-18 models. Evaluating the proposed interpretation through interventions and testing it on larger architectures remain open directions, taken up again in Chapter~\ref{ch:conclusion}.

label: def:maxout_multiplication_network
statement_tex:
[Maxout multiplication network]\label{def:maxout_multiplication_network}
A \emph{rank-$k$ Maxout multiplication network} is a finite directed acyclic graph of \emph{input neurons}, \emph{addition neurons}, and \emph{multiplication neurons}. An addition neuron $v$ carries weight vectors $w^{uv} \in \RR^k$ on its incoming arcs and computes the rank-$k$ Maxout activation $a^v = \max_{i \in [k]} \sum_{u} w^{uv}_i a^u$; a multiplication neuron carries natural exponents $w^{uv} \in \NN$ and computes the monomial $a^v = \prod_{u} (a^u)^{w^{uv}}$. The network is called \emph{monotone} if all weights are non-negative, and \emph{input-convex} if all weights are non-negative except possibly those on arcs leaving input neurons.

label: prop:posynomial_representation
statement_tex:
[Representation by maxima of posynomials, \LeanResult{prop:posynomial_representation}]\label{prop:posynomial_representation}
A monotone rank-$k$ Maxout multiplication network with non-negative intermediate quantities represents the maximum of finitely many posynomials in its non-negative input variables, and is monotone on the non-negative orthant. This representation does not imply ordinary convexity: the positive-coefficient monomial $xy$ is a counterexample. Allowing signed input-incident affine maps likewise supplies no general input-convexity guarantee in the presence of multiplication.
